BLOCKER: `pfaudit.Down` copy-back SELECTs live rows into `audit_legacy` with no post-condition asserting the copied-back count equals the post-swap delta; `RequireUnfilteredVisibility` only covers `audit`/`audit_partitioned`, so an RLS-filtered or differently-owned legacy table can silently strand post-swap events during an emergency rollback.

`reconcile` and `restore` (and their library calls `ReconcileHolds`/`RestoreMonth`) run outside the AURE advisory lock — only export/purge/holds lock — so a concurrent export/drop can race hold extraction and lose legally held rows.
MAJOR: `edpsvc` now imports `pgxpool` directly and opens a fresh pool per `/admin/audit-coverage` request, bypassing the datastore port abstraction and creating unbounded connection churn on a request path.
The documented crash-resume path (`runSwap` observing `StateSwapped`) has no integration test; only `PostVerify` is called directly, so the resume branch in the shipped CLI is unverified.

Active-hold detection is duplicated in four places (`audit_drop_partition`, `audit_approve_purge`, `PurgeMonth`, `DownPlan`) with different formulations; drift would allow a held month to be dropped or purged.
`audit_provision` swallows `exclusion_violation` in addition to `42P07`, masking genuine range-overlap (23P01) defects that AC only sanctions as an attach race.

`AuditStore.Append` classifies failures by substring-matching the error text ("no partition of relation"); brittle across driver/PG versions — use SQLSTATE plus a stable constraint/errdetail discriminator.

Threshold drift: `edpsvc.auditCoverage` hardcodes `48` instead of `PF_AUDIT_ROTATION_MAX_AGE_HOURS`; `pfaudit-retention coverage` hardcodes `< 2` instead of `lead_months` from `audit_partition_config`.
AC requires a fresh-install case (empty audit, `setval` to 1) to be tested; no such test exists in the suite.
MINOR: Freeze budget is evaluated only after the rename has committed and PostVerify ran; an over-budget run exits non-zero post-commit with no distinct state, complicating operator triage.
`audit_swap_freeze_seconds` includes pool acquire and transaction setup, so the measured freeze overstates the true ACCESS EXCLUSIVE window.
Migration 0014 performs DML (`INSERT INTO audit_partition_config`, `setval`) despite the "DDL-only" AC wording.
`close` derives the rollback window from the newest `to_state='swapped'` event, so a crash-resume re-record silently extends the rollback period.

`RestoreMonth` builds batched multi-row INSERTs via string-concatenated placeholder lists; a `fmt`-based approach is fine but the `ON CONFLICT (id, at) DO NOTHING` path can mask a partial restore that the count check then catches only by luck of ordering.
NIT: `pfaudit-retention` emits metrics only on success; `fail()` exits without `emitMetrics`, unlike `pfaudit-swap` which emits on failure paths.

`DefaultSSE()` returning bare `"aws:kms"` is always rejected by `CheckSSE` unless `PF_S3_KMS_KEY` is set — any S3 deployment without the key fails closed by construction; worth documenting explicitly.
`0004_runtime_role.up.sql` was edited in place to become idempotent; environments that track migration checksums would see applied history invalidated.
SUMMARY: Solid, unusually thorough implementation: catalog-driven state detection, ensure-based DDL, privilege-enforced hardening, verified two-stage retention and hold reconciliation are all present and mostly tested. Top risks are the unlocked reconcile/restore path (legal-evidence integrity), the unasserted `--down` copy-back, and the pgxpool shortcut introduced into `edpsvc`.
